title: ElastiCache/Redis CPU and Evictions

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.1.36 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.1.36 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:cloudwatch` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" namespace="AWS/ElastiCache" (metric_name="CPUUtilization" OR metric_name="CacheEvictions")
| table _time metric_name namespace unit average maximum
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.36_elasticache_redis_cpu_an_36"
| sort -_time
description: High CPU or evictions indicate undersized cache or hot keys. Impacts application latency and cache hit ratio.
value: Detecting elasticache/redis cpu and evictions early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Collect ElastiCache metrics per node/cluster. Alert on CPUUtilization > 80% sustained. Monitor CacheHitRate; low hit rate and high evictions suggest need for more memory or key design review.
visualization: Line chart (CPU, evictions, hit rate), Table (cluster, metrics), Gauge (hit rate).
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` max(Performance.cpu_load_percent) as peak
  from datamodel=Performance.All_Performance
  by Performance.object Performance.host span=1h
| where isnotnull(peak)
| sort - peak
dataModelAcceleration: Performance: enable if `aws:cloudwatch` (or your metric store) is mapped to CIM Performance, or use `mstats` on the same CloudWatch metrics. Enable Data Model Acceleration for the CIM data models in `cimModels` once `Splunk_TA_aws` (and any CIM tags/aliases) map your fields; otherwise the `cimSpl` summary search may be empty. Step 2 on raw or metric indexes stays primary for most sites.
knownFalsePositives: Planned deploys, game-day tests, and vendor maintenance that you expect to move CPU, error, or lag metrics; compare with the change window.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:cloudwatch`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.1.78.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `metric_name` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Collect ElastiCache metrics per node/cluster. Alert on CPUUtilization > 80% sustained. Monitor CacheHitRate; low hit rate and high evictions suggest need for more memory or key design review.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" namespace="AWS/ElastiCache" (metric_name="CPUUtilization" OR metric_name="CacheEvictions")
| table _time metric_name namespace unit average maximum
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.36_elasticache_redis_cpu_an_36"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudwatch` in `index=aws` to detect elasticache/redis cpu and evictions. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the Amazon CloudWatch console Metrics for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `metric_name` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_36_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Line chart (CPU, evictions, hit rate), Table (cluster, metrics), Gauge (hit rate)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of elasticache/redis cpu and evictions so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
